newsitem.title: USA: Mobil volume, downstream boosts Q2 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Mobil volume, downstream boosts Q2 earnings.

text.p: Mobil Corp became the latest major oil company to beat analyst forecasts when it reported operating earnings per share of $1.09, up from $1.02 a year ago and ahead of forecasts of $1.01.
The company cited volume growth, strong operating performance at U.S. refineries and improved results in its lubricants business as the reason for its better performance.

The company said that including a special charge of $20 million for start-up costs from its Mobil-British Petroleum Co European downstream alliance, net income for the quarter was $850 million, or $1.06 per share, compared with $783 million, or $0.98 per share, which included a $31 million charge for staff reorganization costs.
Chief executive Lucio Noto said that Mobil had started to see the benefits of its BP alliance.
Marketing and refining income rose to $420 million from $352 million and was up $25 million in the U.S. to $194 million and up $23 million overseas to $206 million.
"These improvements were partly offset by increased refinery downtime in Asia-Pacific and somewhat higher expenses related to new business development, primarily in upstream operations," Noto said.
Exploration and production income slid to $458 million from $470 million, down $40 million in the U.S. to $127 million, but up $28 million overseas to $331 million overseas.
The decline in the U.S. was due to lower volumes from asset sales and field declines as well as lower energy prices.

Mobil said that excluding impact of West Coast realizations for June due to the Shell exploration and production alliance, the average U.S. crude oil prices fell year on year to $16.18 per barrel from $17.12 and natural gas prices fell to $1.88 per thousand cubic feet from $2.05.
Internationally, crude prices fell $2.16 per barrel of crude to $17.34 and natural gas prices rose 13 cents to $2.63.
Net liquids production rose by 87,000 barrels per day (bpd) to 922,000 and natural gas output was 1.72 billion cubic feet per day, up 110 million cubic feet.

Refinery runs in the U.S. rose 39,000 barrels to 978,000 bpd but worldwide, including the U.S. they fell 33,000 bpd to 2.12 billion as Asia-Pacific output fell by 114,000 bpd to 574,000 bpd due to downtime at the refineries.
Chemical segment adjusted net income rose $26 million to $91 million in the quarter.

Mobil's Noto said that the company would continue to manage its business in a world where "business fundamentals are unpredictable in the near term and cannot be relies upon to sustain or improve earnings".
